jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Reporting & Analytics
jobs.desc:
**About RocketRez:**  
RocketRez is the revenue maximization platform behind boat tours, theme parks, zoos, and other attractions and experience operators. Operators run their businesses on us: ticketing, capacity, memberships, point of sale, web stores, and the data that tells them how how to grow their business.
  
  
**The role:**  
Operators ask us questions every day. How did yesterday go? Which channel actually converts? Did the new pricing pay off, or did it just move demand around? Your job is to turn those questions into data, reports, and visuals that answer them clearly and lead to a revenue maximizing decision.
  
**You'll own Reporting & Analytics end to end:** the reports, dashboards, and insights operators use to run their business, from the general manager checking yesterday's attendance to the finance lead reconciling a month of revenue across channels, and the data models and metric definitions behind them. You'll own its roadmap, its customers, and the case for where engineering time goes. Your job is to prove that reporting can be the front door to RocketRez: where operators start their day, and what moves them to act. You'll be measured on usage, and on the revenue operators earn from the decisions reporting drives.
  
  
**What we're building:**  
Operators move more of their business onto RocketRez when they trust us with their busiest day, and that trust depends on the numbers. If the reporting is wrong, late, or confusing, nothing else we build gets believed.
  
First, reporting operators trust. Core reporting on par with the best in hospitality.
  
Next, a revenue engine. Operators set revenue targets and campaigns, track their pace against them and against past seasons, and get clear options when they fall behind.
  
Then, automated revenue management. Automation keeps tracking and planning running without the operator asking. It recommends actions grounded in the operator's own history and in how similar operators are performing, and makes acting on them a single click. Season pass sales dipping? Here are three options based on this season and the last two.
  
  
**What you'll do:**  
Understand the question• Spend real time with operators across roles, from general managers and finance leads to marketers and front-gate supervisors. Learn the decisions they make and the questions they need answered to make them.
  

* Design reporting that leads to a decision. Every report should make clear what it means and what to do next.

Data fluency• Prototype with real data. Write your own SQL to mock up a report or metric and put it in front of operators before engineering builds it.
  

* Own the metric definitions the platform runs on: revenue, attendance, capacity utilization, and conversion mean the same thing in every report, in every domain.
* Apply statistical judgment: seasonality, small samples, cohorts, fair comparisons, and forecasting.
* Choose the right visual for the question, and hold a high bar for clarity, accuracy, and honest scales.
* Treat data quality as product quality.
* Work with other domains so new products capture the data reporting needs before they ship.

**Strategy and roadmap• Own the roadmap:** sizing, sequencing, and what gets cut.
  

* Shape how automation and AI turn insights into recommended actions: which recommendations are trustworthy, when a human should decide, and the guardrails around both.
* Define how cross-operator benchmarks work: peer sets, minimum sample sizes, and anonymization that operators trust enough to opt into.
* Make the build, buy, and partner calls on analytics tooling, and know the market well enough to say which gaps are worth closing.

**What we look for:**  
The trait we care about most is adaptability. The tools and methods of product management are changing, so we hire people who have already reinvented how they work on their own initiative and will do it again.
  

* You've rebuilt how you work without being told to, including becoming AI-na

With ICyte, Life Sciences innovators can digitalize their market access operations, freeing up resources to focus on more data-driven decision support. We are headquartered in Philadelphia, PA (USA), with offices in: Ambler, PA (USA); Pune, India; and Medellín, Colombia. For more information, visit www.integrichain.com, or follow us on Twitter @IntegriChain and LinkedIn.

To be successful in this role, there are some requirements to visit our office locations from quarterly to a few times a quarter for workshops, team meetings and collaboration between teams. There will be opportunity for international travel annually or as needed based on business needs.

 **Job Description**

**Mission**

IntegriChain is on a mission to help all stakeholders in the life sciences industry drive access. We do this through our relentless focus on unifying all of the critical business functions for therapy commercialization and access contracts and pricing, gross-to-net, channel, and patient services unlocking strategic payer, provider, pharmacy and patient access insights for our life sciences customers.

This role is for a **Sr. Product Manager who wants real ownership and real impact**. You will own a critical product area end‑to‑end—**from problem discovery through delivery and adoption**—with clear accountability for outcomes, not just execution. You’ll operate as a decision‑maker at the center of Product, Engineering, QA, Operations, and customer‑facing teams, shaping strategy while staying deeply connected to how the product is built and used.

The problems you’ll work on are **complex, operationally critical, and deeply embedded in customer workflows**. You’ll be expected to challenge assumptions, prioritize based on evidence, and make hard tradeoffs when constraints collide.

* Lead release planning and readiness for assigned product

jobs.title: Senior Technical Product Manager, IT Service Management
jobs.desc:
Our mission at Oura is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.

Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.

We are looking for a hands-on Senior Technical Product Manager to own Oura's IT service management (ITSM) and employee service management (ESM) platforms. You will lead our move off a legacy ITSM tool to a modern, AI-native platform, then bring service management to teams like HR, Finance, Legal, and Security on whichever platform or platforms fit them best. You will be fluent in ITSM theory, comfortable evaluating tools without bias, and willing to roll up your sleeves to configure, integrate, and ship. Above all, you will care about the people on the other side of every request and work to make getting help easy and seamless.

### **What You Will Do:**

* Lead the migration from our legacy ITSM platform to a modern, AI-native one, from data model, workflow, and catalog design through integrations, cutover, and decommission, with no loss in service levels or employee satisfaction
* Be the voice of the employee. Design requests, catalog items, and knowledge from the worker's point of view so getting help is easy and frictionless, and use feedback and service data to keep removing friction
* Own the platform as a product: a single roadmap and backlog, clear intake, and prioritization criteria that every service team can see and trust
* Govern the service catalog and request fulfillment. Decide what gets added, changed, or retired, and move requests from manual work toward automated and identity-governed fulfillment
* Own the knowledge management function: the standards, structure, and governance that make knowledge accurate and findable for people and AI agents alike, while individual teams keep ownership of their own content
* Define how AI agents operate in service management: which requests they resolve, which they route to a human, and the accuracy thresholds and guardrails behind each
* Build a repeatable onboarding model for ESM so non-IT service teams can adopt a consistent service experience, whichever platform fits them (intake, catalog, workflows, knowledge, reporting, access controls)
* Keep the platform audit-ready by designing change, incident, and access workflows that produce the evidence our SOX, SOC 2, and HIPAA controls require
* Work hands-on in the platform and with engineers on configuration, integrations, and automation, and direct vendor and partner work where needed

This is a remote role based in the US.

### **What you'll bring**

* 6+ years in IT service management, service platform, or internal-tools product roles
* Led at least one end-to-end ITSM or ESM tool implementation or migration through go-live
* Strong grounding in ITSM concepts and practices (ITIL or equivalent), and the judgment to evaluate platforms on their merits rather than loyalty to one vendor
* Hands-on depth with a modern service management platform, including service catalog, workflow and SLA configuration, knowledge management, and reporting
* Experience with an AI-native ITSM platform (such as Atomicwork or Serval), or with Jira Service Management, Freshservice, or similar
* Working knowledge of ServiceNow, including its data model, workflows, and administration, and how to get data and configuration back out of it
* Experience designing access-request and fulfillment workflows integrated with an identity provider or identity governance platform
* Experience applying AI

### **Who We Are**

Cobalt was founded on the belief of a fundamental human aspiration: the desire to live better and safer. It all started in 2013, when our founders realized that pentesting can be better. Today our diverse, fully remote team is committed to helping organizations of all sizes with seamless, effective and collaborative Offensive Security Testing that empower organizations to OPERATE FEARLESSLY and INNOVATE SECURELY.

Our customers can start a pentest in as little as 24 hours and integrate with advanced development cycles thanks to the powerful combination of our SaaS platform and an exclusive community of testers known as the Cobalt Core. Accepting just 5% of applicants, the Cobalt Core boasts over 400 closely vetted and highly skilled testers who jointly conduct thousands of tests each year and are at the forefront of identifying and helping remediate risk across a dynamically changing attack surface.

Cobalt is an equal-opportunity employer, and we strive to build a diverse and inclusive workforce. At Cobalt, we aspire to engage with diverse individuals, communities, and organizations to continue to nurture our unique, rich, diverse culture. Join our team, and be your true self to do your best work.

**Description**

Modern software demands continuous security validation. Cobalt is pioneering the evolution beyond legacy, point-in-time PTaaS through our Autonomous and Continuous pentesting platform-providing continuous, scalable, and AI-driven security coverage across enterprise environments.

In the role of **Senior Technical Product Manager**, you will shape the strategic product vision, steer live initiatives, and spearhead 0-to-1 feature development to drive business ROI across Cobalt's Autonomous and Continuous Pentesting portfolio. You will conduct deep product discovery, instill scalable PM leadership practices, and redefine how continuous, autonomous offensive security is delivered to modern enterprises.

You will combine strong business acumen with technical rigor, driving clear feature ownership from discovery to delivery. Operating as a proactive cross-functional leader, you will challenge existing processes and communicate transparently to ensure our continuous pentesting platform solves critical customer security problems with measurable impact.

**What You Would Do**

As a member of a growing team of product managers your responsibilities include:

* **Strategic PM Leadership & Business ROI:** Own the product vision, roadmap, and delivery for the Autonomous and Continuous pentesting portfolio. Align feature scope directly with customer value and measurable business outcomes, tracking clear adoption and retention metrics.
* **Product Discovery Excellence:** Lead continuous customer discovery and market validation to identify high-impact customer problems in the continuous security testing space. Translate complex user needs into actionable, validated product requirements.
* **End-to-End Feature Ownership:** Take full operational ownership of product features across the entire lifecycle—from initial ideation and specification to execution, deployment, and post-launch evaluation.
* **Proactive Leadership & Process Innovation:** Actively challenge inefficient workflows, implement scalable product processes, and foster high alignment across engineering, design, marketing, and executive stakeholders.
* **Transparent & Structured Communication:** Maintain standard executive-level visibility into roadmap progress, product decisions, and operational metrics through regular updates and clear artifact documentation.
* **Domain Expertise in Autonomous Security:** Serve as the internal subject matter expert on continuous vulnerability management, AI-driven offensive security techniques, and automated pentesting workflows.
* **Data-Driven Performance Management:** Define and monitor rigorous success criteria, evaluating product performance against strategic business metrics and customer satisfaction outcomes.

Freight forwarders, customs brokers, carriers, and 3PLs touch millions of shipments and connect shippers, suppliers, and governments. The LSP Platform team builds the products that enable keeping up with the rapid pace of government regulation, and modernizing the business processes by engaging in Altana's network. With these tools, LSPs can run a fully agentic, collaborative and cutting edge customs process covering everything needed to screen and clear shipments faster, protect their customers from risk and delays, and offer new trade intelligence services to the shippers they serve.

As Senior Product Manager for the LSP Platform, you'll own the roadmap for one of Altana's most strategic product areas. You'll work directly with some of the world's largest logistics companies to understand how goods move, where compliance and risk create friction, and how Altana can remove it. Your job is to embed Altana into the daily workflows of LSPs so it works as a native capability. You'll also turn LSPs into multipliers for the Altana network.

You'll partner with engineering, design, data science, and our go-to-market teams to ship features that make a measurable difference for customers. You'll be accountable for adoption, usage, and customer outcomes.

  

**You Will**

* Write clear requirements engineers can build from, and prototype with AI to test ideas before production code is written.

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager, Confluence Aggregation
jobs.desc:
Overview:

**Working at Atlassian**

Atlassians can choose where they work – whether in an office, from home, or a combination of the two. That way, Atlassians have more control over supporting their family, personal goals, and other priorities. We can hire people in any country where we have a legal entity.

Responsibilities:

**About the team**
------------------

Confluence is where organizations write down what they know: decisions, architecture, process, and policy. But a company's work does not happen in one tool. It happens in file drives, chat, code hosts, CRMs, and data platforms.

The Aggregation team makes Confluence fill and organize itself from those tools. Content arrives with its source system's permissions intact, gets organized so a team can navigate it, and stays current as the underlying work changes. That content is what Confluence's AI answers are built on, which makes its coverage and quality the difference between an answer a team acts on and one they go verify by hand.

**About the role**
------------------

You will own how Confluence turns connected content into knowledge that maintains itself: what a space pulls in, how it gets organized, how it stays current, and when it flags that something important is missing. Vision through launch and iteration, on problems that arrive undefined.

Quality is the job here, not a stage of it. Content that is stale, mis-grouped, or wrong does more damage than content that was never connected at all, because a team will have already acted on it.

You are building for three audiences, and the role requires you to name which one you are serving in every decision: the admin who approves connecting a system of record and will disconnect it the moment trust breaks, the space owner accountable for a body of knowledge staying current, and the end user who wants the answer without knowing which tool it came from.

### **What you'll do**

* Own the strategy and roadmap for what connected content becomes inside Confluence: what gets pulled in, how it is grouped, titled, and summarized, and what happens to content that has gone stale or contradicts a published page.
* Define how messy inputs become usable structure. Documents, spreadsheets, meeting transcripts, chat threads, and CRM records do not arrive as pages, and deciding what shape they take in Confluence is the core of the work.
* Own freshness and decay. Decide what updates on its own when a source changes, what needs a human to confirm, and how a user can tell which one they are looking at.

1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access. We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that.

But we're going further. Over 75,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 1 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens.

We're a Series D company with $325M+ in funding (a16z, Accel, Spark Capital, etc.), looking for exceptional people to help us achieve this mission. We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better.

About This Role:

Every month, hundreds of thousands of patients and providers interact with Headway's support systems. Today, most interactions are handled by human agents working across disconnected tools. We believe CX is a product, not just a department — and the right product leader can transform how Headway supports its customers while dramatically improving both satisfaction and cost efficiency.

As Director of Product for CX, you will build Headway's CX product function from the ground up. You'll own the product vision and strategy for how patients and providers get help — from AI-powered self-resolution to context-aware agent tooling to the feedback loops that connect support insights back to the product.

You will:

  • Define the vision and strategy for Headway's CX product — spanning AI-powered resolution, agent tooling, proactive engagement, channel strategy, knowledge systems, and the feedback loops that connect support insights back to the product.
  • Build and lead a team of product managers focused on reducing cost-to-serve while increasing resolution quality and customer satisfaction.
  • Own the AI resolution layer — build the agentic workflows and API integrations that enable the AI agent to actually resolve problems, not just answer questions. Define the autonomy framework: what AI handles without human involvement, what needs guardrails, and what requires a human.
  • Build proactive engagement — systems that contact customers before they discover problems. Shift Headway's CX from reactive to proactive.
  • Launch and unify all contact channels — email, text, and voice — with intelligent routing that delivers differentiated experiences based on customer context, value, and issue type.
  • Own the knowledge and quality layer — machine-readable SOPs, AI evaluation frameworks and crisis escalation pathways.
  • Partner deeply with CX Operations to build agent tooling that makes human agents dramatically more effective — AI copilot, full journey context, auto-generated summaries.
  • Close the feedback loop: build the system that identifies the highest-impact product defects driving support volume and surfaces them to insurance platform teams for upstream fixes.
  • Establish measurement frameworks that connect CX product investments to business outcomes..

jobs.title: Head of Product @ Koast.ai
jobs.desc:
Head of Product | Contract, 20 hrs/week to start, growing into full-time | Remote (US overlapping hours) | Reports to the CEO

The short version

Koast is the AI operating layer for teams that run Meta ads at volume. Agencies, in-house media buying teams, and enterprise buyers managing 10+ ad accounts and launching 50+ ads a week use Koast to launch faster, automate optimizations off real attribution data, and see every account from one hub. The Koast Agent is the next layer: an AI that reads the account, spots what matters, and acts inside guardrails.

We are a small team shipping fast. The product is live, customers are paying, a Whop partnership just onboarded a wave of new users, and the Agent build is underway. What we do not have is one person who owns the product end to end: what gets built, why, in what order, and whether it actually landed.

That is this role. It starts at 20 hours a week on contract. If you are the right person, it becomes the full-time product seat at Koast.

What you will own

Discovery that finds the real problem. You will sit in on enterprise sales calls and onboarding sessions, run discovery with agencies and media buying teams, and figure out what they are actually trying to get done versus what they say they want. Every feature request gets mapped to a job: launching smoother, getting their team in, getting tasks done, keeping users active and growing spend inside Koast. If it does not serve a job, it does not get built.

Specs that engineering can execute without a meeting. We run a lean engineering team plus an AI-assisted dev pipeline. That only works when the ticket is unambiguous. You will write PRDs and Shortcut tickets that define the behavior, the edge cases, the data dependencies (Meta API limits, Hyros and Cometly attribution feeds, Whop account provisioning), and the acceptance criteria. If an engineer or an agent has to guess, the spec was not done.

The queue, and what is missing from it. You own the Up Next column. You will keep engineering fed so they are never blocked, and you will keep a standing view of what is discussed in Slack, support, and QA that does not yet have a ticket. Gaps are your problem before they become customer problems.

Evidence over opinion. PostHog, Intercom, session replays, rage clicks, support threads. You will run the user-behavior audit, know where people drop off in launching, and bring numbers to every prioritization argument, including the ones with the CEO.

Delivery from spec to shipped. Governance, milestones, release notes, and the customer conversation after it ships. When something breaks or slips, you are the one who says so early, not the one who explains it after.

Technical judgement in a non-deterministic product. The Koast Agent makes decisions off data that is noisy, seasonal, and shaped by Meta's learning phase. You will make product calls that respect that: what the Agent is allowed to do, what it must never do, how we measure whether an automated action was correct. Guardrails are infrastructure here, not UI. You need to understand why.

What you will do week to week

  • Run discovery sessions with prospects and customers and turn them into scoped, execution-ready PRDs.
  • Surface technical risk early: undocumented API behavior, missing data, an assumption that will not survive a real ad account.
  • Write and groom Shortcut tickets with enough detail for an engineer or Claude Code to ship without a follow-up question.
  • Partner with engineering on feasibility, sequencing, and cutting scope to what ships this week.
  • Own success metrics per feature and report on them after launch, n

**About DriveCentric**

* Founded in 2010 and headquartered in St. Louis, MO, with a distributed team across the US.
* Backed by Summit Partners, with a mandate to grow, not to trim.
* Trusted by 3,300+ dealerships across the US and Canada, from single-store independents to multi-billion-dollar dealer groups, plus adjacent retail such as RV, marine and powersports.

Three things are true at once:

* The portfolio is multiplying. We are moving from one product line to a platform spanning sales, service, data, F&I, payments and digital retail. Each department has a different buyer, a different competitor set and a different vocabulary. Nobody owns the messaging architecture that ties them together.

* Product velocity is ahead of field readiness. Engineering and product are shipping at a pace the company has never operated at. Sales, account management, onboarding and support need enablement that is timely, credible and actually used, and we do not yet have the system to produce it.

* The category is up for grabs. The market wants to put us in the CRM box. Our thesis is that AI agents change what "CRM" means, and the company that explains that best to a skeptical, relationship-driven buyer wins the next decade of auto retail software. That story needs an owner.

jobs.desc:
**Director, Product Management (PrintOps)**  
**Pharos | US Remote**

  
  
*Here's what you'd actually be stepping into: an established product, two new markets it hasn't reached yet, and no one left who can tell you why it behaves the way it does. Some people need that explanation handed to them. Others go dig it up themselves. This role is for the second kind.*

### About Pharos

Pharos Systems International is the leader in PrintOps, the integrated, user-centric, and cloud-native approach to managing printing and the infrastructure and operations behind it. Pharos' modern print management software empowers enterprises to reduce costs, strengthen security, and support today's hybrid workforce with simple, reliable, and scalable printing solutions. Trusted by thousands of organizations, including many of the world's largest Fortune 500 companies, Pharos has helped eliminate print servers, cut millions in print-related spend, and accelerate the transition to cloud-based infrastructure. Headquartered in Rochester, NY, Pharos has been delivering innovative print management solutions and measurable ROI since 1992.  
  
Our flagship product already runs inside a large, established customer base, which means it carries real history, real workarounds, and a level of hidden complexity that isn't written down anywhere. We're also pushing it into new markets it hasn't served before, without losing the trust of the customers who already rely on it every day. That combination, protecting what works while extending what's possible, is exactly why this role exists.

### What This Role Is

This role owns the full product loop for one of Pharos's most established product areas: understanding how it actually works today, bringing its capabilities under control, deciding what to build and what to explicitly leave alone, and making sure Engineering and the rest of the company are working from the same understanding you are.  
  
You'll work directly with enterprise customers, including the conversations where the answer is no, and you'll set direction across customer commitments, technical constraints, and two new markets at once, without letting the loudest voice in the room decide the roadmap for you.  
  
You'll also use AI as a normal part of how you work: discovery, synthesis, competitive research, epic drafting, documentation, not as a novelty, but as how the work actually gets done, in a fast loop with Engineering that doesn't wait on oversized specs.

### What You Will Own

* The model of how this product actually works, and keeping it current as you learn more.
* A visible roadmap where every item has a reason, an owner, and a real answer for what Pharos is and isn't doing.
* The path from a raw signal (a support ticket, a sales request, a customer complaint) to a decision someone can act on.
* Direct conversations with enterprise customers, including the ones where the answer is no.
* The translation of product direction into work Engineering can actually build and verify against.
* Making sure Sales, Support, Customer Success, Services, and Marketing know what changed and why, not just that it changed.

### What a Strong Background Looks Like

* You've owned a mature, complicated product, one with real history, real workarounds, and a real customer base, not just a green-field build.
* You've sat across the table from enterprise customers directly: discovery calls, pilots, advisory relationships, the uncomfortable ones included.
* You've turned a messy customer or market need into something Engineering could actually build against, and stuck around to see what happened after.
* You've made a complex product simpler, more consistent, or easier to reason about, not just added more to it.
* You reach for AI as a normal part of how you think through a problem, not as a novelty.

**Not a good fit if…**

**Strong fit if…**

  

You're looking to build and lead a team starting now.  
You've only ever built new products from a blank sheet,

### About Pharos

Pharos Systems International is the leader in PrintOps, the integrated, user-centric, and cloud-native approach to managing printing and the infrastructure and operations behind it. Pharos' modern print management software empowers enterprises to reduce costs, strengthen security, and support today's hybrid workforce with simple, reliable, and scalable printing solutions. Pharos has an early proof of concept in security and real conviction about where the market is headed. What we don't have yet is proof it holds up at scale, or a repeatable way to turn that thesis into a validated business. That gap is exactly why this role exists.

### What This Role Is

This role owns the full loop from thesis to revenue: understanding who the real buyer is and what they'll actually pay to solve, turning an existing proof of concept into something multiple customers can rely on, and building the go-to-market motion that gets it from a handful of pilots to a repeatable business.  
  
You'll work directly with Engineering, not just direct it: prototyping, reviewing technical tradeoffs, and getting into implementation details yourself when that's the fastest way to learn something. You'll also work directly with customers and, over time, with Sales, to turn early proof into paying accounts.  
  
You'll report directly to the CEO, with the autonomy that comes with that and the visibility too. There's no team here yet. What you build, you build largely with your own judgment and your own hands.

* The market thesis: who the real buyer is, what they're actually willing to pay for, and what this product will deliberately not attempt.
* The path from an early proof of concept to something multiple paying customers can rely on.
* Direct, hands-on work with Engineering: epics, prototypes, requirements, and implementation tradeoffs.
* The go-to-market motion: positioning, packaging, pricing input, and what it takes to turn a pilot into a paying customer.
* A fast, honest read on what's working and what isn't, reported straight to the CEO, without waiting for a perfect plan to have that conversation.

### What a Strong Background Looks Like

* You've built and shipped something close to zero to one, not just contributed to an already-mature product line.
* You've worked directly with customers to test whether a problem is real and worth paying to solve, not just gathered requirements secondhand.
* You've gotten into the technical details yourself: a prototype, a proof of concept, a spec you wrote and then helped build.
* You've made a real call with incomplete information and lived with the outcome, good or bad.
* You reach for AI as a normal part of how you think through a problem, not as a novelty.

You're comfortable being the person who validates the market, not just executing inside one someone else already proved.

  

Your best work has come from directing others rather than building things yourself.

You still want to be hands-on with prototypes and implementation, not just strategy.

**Director of Product**  
Team: Product  
Reports to: McKay Ferrell, CPO  
Location: Remote, United States  
Type: Full-time  
  
Job Summary  
As a Director of Product at SureCost, you'll own the business of a set of products that pharmacies  
depend on to keep drugs on the shelf at the right cost. You'll bring new products to market and make  
our existing products better, from the first customer conversation through launch and adoption. You'll  
know our customers well enough to build things they love to use, and you'll measure whether they do.  
This is a hands-on role. You'll talk to customers every week, prototype ideas before engineering builds  
them, and work with our commercial team to launch and sell what we ship. We're rebuilding how our  
product team works around AI tools, and you'll help shape that as you go.  
  
Essential Functions  

* Own the roadmap, outcomes and quarterly priorities for your product areas, and decide which

initiatives make the quarter within the capacity your pods actually have.  

* Run a monthly business review for your area covering adoption, customer issues, revenue signals

and delivery against plan.  

* Build toward product-level P&L visibility for your area with the CPO.
* Own the quality of what your area ships, including the share of engineering time that goes to various

initiatives.  

* Build and help guide product builder team members with AI tooling and structures.
* Stay close to customers. Expect several customer conversations a week, including the hard ones

with enterprise accounts.  

* Work with the commercial team on product launch planning and enablement, including launch

timing, sales training, demo readiness and customer communication.  

* Partner with Marketing on positioning, messaging and competitive intelligence for your products.
* Give pricing and packaging input for new products and major enhancements.
* Bring what you hear from Sales, Customer Success and the market back into the roadmap, including

win/loss patterns and competitor moves.  

* Track adoption after launch and work with Customer Success to drive it.
* Build and ship prototypes, skills and agents yourself, and set the standard your team follows for AI-

assisted discovery, specs and evaluation.  

* Own the AI agents in your area end to end: the problem they solve, the precision bar they have to

meet, the evaluation that proves it, and where a named human approves an action.  

* Recommend when to stop or reshape an initiative, and bring the evidence.

SureCost | Job Description  

* Work across product areas with the other Director, Product Ops and Design so the product lifecycle

(inventory, purchasing, shortage) holds together for the customer.  
  
How We Work  

* Product areas own the work. Our value streams point where our teams are focused and set how

each pod's hours are split, and every Director plans inside that split.  

* Our product builders combine what used to be PM, PO and UX roles. Agents draft stories,

acceptance criteria, status and first-pass triage. People make the decisions and own the quality.  

* AI fluency is part of how we hire and how we review.
* We're remote-first. Most of our work takes place over digital ecosystems, including video calls,

chats, email, and other systems – you’ll need to be self-motivated and comfortable in an all-remote  
environment.  

* The domain is complicated: GPO contracts, wholesaler operations, DSCSA, 340B and drug shortages.

We give you time to learn it, and we expect you to go deep.  
  
Requirements

This is a player/coach role and you should be skilled at driving outcomes as an individual contributor at times. You will leverage your technical depth to partner credibly with principal data engineers while applying strong business judgment and executive storytelling to connect job inventory health, latency, and quality directly to platform engagement, SEO footprint, and monetization.

**About this team**

Job Ingestion is the foundational engine that powers BOLD's entire job discovery and recruitment platform. Our mission is to build, scale, and optimize high-throughput, enterprise-grade ingestion systems that aggregate, parse, normalize, and index millions of job postings daily across all BOLD properties and partner feeds. By transforming high-volume, unstructured job data into rich, standardized job entities, our team enables critical downstream capabilities – most notably powering Search & Match, job alerts, SEO landing pages, recommendations, and employer analytics. We operate at the intersection of Data Engineering, Core Infrastructure, Search & Match, and Enterprise GTM to ensure job content is accurate, fresh, comprehensive, and instantly accessible to job seekers globally.

* Executive Storytelling & Alignment: Translate technical data concepts (pipeline latency, schema health, ATS stability) into executive-ready business narratives and clear investment proposals for leadership.
* Cross-Functional Partnership: Build trust and alignment across matrixed teams, including Data Engineering, Search & Match, SEO, Portal, Mobile, and Job Alerts, to ensure seamless integration of normalized job content into all downstream surfaces.
* Operational & Technical Execution: Lead cross-functional squads (data engineers, PMs, QA) to drive predictable delivery, establishing rigorous metrics for pipeline uptime, parsing accuracy, deduping precision, and data freshness.
* Data Quality & Governance: Establish schema validation, content freshness, spam/scam detection, and compliance standards to maintain high job catalog health without breaking downstream search indices.
* Team Development & Product Rituals: Coach and mentor product managers in business sense and executive communication, while establishing operational rituals that drive velocity and clarity.

* 8–10+ years of product management experience (or equivalent technical leadership experience) leading complex, large-scale data platforms, ETL/ELT pipelines, scraping/crawling engines, or event-driven data architectures.
* Deep Data Background: Strong technical depth in data engineering foundations (e.g., former Data Engineer, Systems Architect, or Technical PM in data platforms). Hands-on familiarity with structured/unstructured data extraction, schema design, distributed processing, and cloud ecosystem components (AWS, GCP, Kafka, Snowflake).

--------------------------------

Working at Citi is far more than just a job. A career with us means joining a team of approximately 219,000 dedicated people from around the globe. At Citi, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your career, give back to your community and make a real impact.

**Job Overview**
----------------

Citi's U.S. Consumer Cards (USCC) business is one of the largest card issuers in the United States, serving millions of customers across a broad portfolio of branded, cobrand, and retail services card products. The Digital & Client Experience (DCX) team sits at the heart of USCC's strategy. DCX has two mandates. Firstly, we are committed to creating exceptional digital experiences that drive customers to choose digital-first engagement, deepen satisfaction, and fuel commercial growth. With over 2 billion annual mobile sessions and an ambitious roadmap spanning AI-powered servicing, digital acquisition, and channel excellence, DCX is transforming how customers discover, apply for, and engage with Citi's products across the full consumer franchise. Secondly, the CX team within DCX has horizontal accountability for the overall client experience of USCC customers—driving meaningful change cross-functionally.

The Head of Product Strategy, Research & Partner Engagement is a senior leadership role responsible for defining the strategic direction of DCX. This leader serves as a key strategic advisor to DCX leadership, translating consumer needs, competitive trends, emerging technologies, and product performance data into actionable priorities that drive product innovation, investment decisions, and business growth. This role shapes Citi’s digital and CX roadmaps.

Additionally, this leader serves as the senior relationship owner for DCX's key stakeholders. They and their Partner Engagement team act as the connective tissue between DCX and Citi's Card portfolios, Wealth and Retail businesses, as well as functional partners across Marketing, Risk and Operations. This team is responsible for aligning priorities, investment decisions, roadmaps, performance metrics, and business outcomes across a highly matrixed organization.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead the Product Strategy, Research & Partner Engagement function (approximate team size of 15-20), integrating customer research, market intelligence, competitive analysis, business performance metrics, and digital product insights into a cohesive strategic narrative that informs roadmaps, investment decisions, and executive priorities.
* Develop and maintain a forward-looking product strategy framework that identifies emerging customer needs, market opportunities, technology trends, competitive threats, and innovation opportunities.
* Evaluate emerging technologies, including AI-enabled capabilities, and assess their potential impact on customer experience, product innovation, operational effectiveness, and business performance.
* Serve as the primary strategic interface between DCX and key business partners, including Branded Cards, Co-Brand teams, Marketing, Risk, Operations, Wealth, and Retail Bank fostering alignment around priorities, investments, roadmap decisions, and business outcomes.
* Lead executive engagement routines and governance forums that facilitate transparent decision-making, strategic alignment, and resolution of competing priorities across the organization.

Overview:

**Working at Atlassian**

Atlassians can choose where they work – whether in an office, from home, or a combination of the two. That way, Atlassians have more control over supporting their family, personal goals, and other priorities. We can hire people in any country where we have a legal entity.  
  
This role is based in the United States, with Pacific or Mountain time zone strongly preferred to support collaboration with teams in Australia. You should expect regular travel to Sydney, San Francisco, and Seattle.  
  
**About the Role**

Atlassian is reimagining the future of teamwork with AI at its core. Jira’s mission is to autonomously organize, plan, and track work for our customers, then supply context from Atlassian’s Teamwork Graph to agents that help get the work done.

We’re looking for a visionary **Head of Product for Jira** to lead the product organization responsible for Jira’s experience, AI, and customer adoption. In this role, you’ll shape the surfaces where humans and agents work together: work items, boards, lists, backlogs, plans, agent sessions, and the Teamwork Graph context that makes Jira agents uniquely powerful.

You’ll lead a global team of product managers across Australia, the United States, and India. Reporting to Jira’s Head of Product, you’ll operate as an immediate deputy, directly responsible for strategy, team building, and executing major initiatives. You’ll work closely with engineering and design leadership across Atlassian, spend meaningful time with customers, and hold a high quality bar for everything we ship.

Responsibilities:

* **Product Leadership:** Own the multi-year product strategy for how humans and agents do work together in Jira, including new teamwork patterns that emerge as agents take on a larger share of delivery.

* **Team Leadership:** Build, develop, and scale a large product organization, hiring, coaching, leveling, and managing product managers and PM managers across three geographies.
* **Product Craft:** Set the bar for experience-led product management inside Jira, with a focus on taste, prototype-first thinking, and protecting quality by cutting scope when needed.
* **Cross-Functional Partnership:** Partner with leaders across Atlassian, especially in the Teamwork Collection and AI groups, resolving duplicated work and aligning teams around shared outcomes.
* **Customer & Market Voice:** Act as the senior product voice with customers and in the market, translating what you learn from real teams into a durable experience vision.

jobs.title: Head of Product
jobs.desc:
**Type::** Full-time

**Location:** Remote, with a preference for candidates located in NY, TX, MD, or GA

**Compensation:** $140,000 - $180,000

**Job Level:** Director/VP (depending on experience)

**ABOUT LEMONTREE**
-------------------

There are more food pantries in the US than there are McDonalds, but most families facing hunger don't take that help. That's why we started Lemontree–because it makes no sense for our neighbors to go hungry when there's free food around the corner. We've helped one million households access the free food in their communities by bringing technology + empathy to the experience of food assistance. Learn more about us at https://www.foodhelpline.org/about.

### **Our Values**

**Service Over Self**

We put the mission — helping people find food — ahead of ego, credit, or agenda. That means caring for the people we serve and the team around us, and going the extra mile when it makes a real difference. We're here for the work itself and what it makes possible for others.

**Ownership**

We get shit done and we carry our piece so the whole team can move forward. When we make a mistake, we name it early and openly, because a problem we've owned out loud is one we can fix together. In a growing org, this kind of autonomy & accountability is how we do big things with a small team.

**Curiosity**  
We don't take anything for granted. We stay curious about our users and ourselves. We stay humble enough to accept that there's always room to improve. We stay ready to change course when the evidence points somewhere new. The plan we have today is a strong draft, but we'll always need to adapt to a changing world. We'd rather ask the better question and adjust than defend a stale answer.

**THE POSITION**
----------------

Lemontree is looking for a **Head of Product** **& Technology** that will partner with the Executive Director to own and evolve our platform strategy to scale our impact. Since 2020, we've grown from a simple helpline into a platform that serves thousands of families, partners, and volunteers daily. What we need now is someone who can shepherd us to the next level, bringing rigor and direction to how we evolve: sharper prioritization, better use of our data, and clearer decision-making & process around where we invest our resources. Every decision we make should align with our strategic anchors:

* User-centered

* Hospitality in every interaction

* Built for scale

This is a hands-on leadership role with high trust and high agency, reporting to the Executive Director. You'll be the person setting product direction and leading the charge to move it forward, partnering with an engineering agency on execution and collaborating closely across our broader Lemontree team. While product ownership is the focus, this is a multi-disciplinary position that combines product management, data analysis, and technical leadership to build toward stability *and* scalability. If you like operating with real autonomy and are motivated to take things from 1 100, this role will suit you.

### **What You'll Do**

Drive **technical leadership** that delivers a reliable, joyful, scalable user experience for neighbors looking for food assistance.

* Serve as a credible technical voice in conversations about architecture, tradeoffs, and feasibility.
* Direct our engineering agency, translating product priorities into well-scoped technical work and holding a high bar for what ships.
* Oversee third party services that support our product, including setting up integrations, managing billing, negotiating nonprofit discounts, etc.

Own a **product roadmap** that increases the breadth & depth of our impact, aligned with our organizational strategy.

* Partner with CEO & senior leadership to shape overall strategy & product direction. Rather than making every single product decision, you will own the process that helps those decisions happen with the right information, clear accountability, and strong follow-through.

* Innovation with results that matter
* Deliver what you promise
* Can-do attitude
* Open, direct & respectful communications
* We care deeply
* We practice humility

Deque experts regularly contribute to W3C Accessibility Working Groups and collectively hold more CPACC, WAS, & CPWA certifications issued by the IAAP than any accessibility testing company in the world.

**Position Description**

The **Director of Product Management** sets product strategy and vision, drives continuous discovery, and ensures the delivery team is focused on the highest-value work aligned to customer needs, company strategy, and long-term product direction.

This role serves as the connective point between customers, Product Development, Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, and leadership — and is a key voice in shaping how Deque's product organization operates and grows. The ideal candidate combines strong customer empathy, strategic thinking, commercial awareness, and execution discipline in a fast-paced B2B SaaS environment, and is energized by helping other PMs grow.

This role is a peer of other director, and senior director positions, leads product managers and product owners, and is expected to operate as a leader of leaders within a leadership team: running some department and cross-company forums, forming strong relationships with peers across the organization and with senior executives, and evaluating how product resources are deployed across the portfolio.

**Primary Responsibilities**

* Own product strategy and vision, ensuring it aligns with company strategy and the competitive landscape.
* Continuously engage with customers, users, Sales, Support, and Customer Success to be the embodiment of the product's target market for the rest of the development team.
* Own and prioritize the product roadmap, ensuring teams focus on the highest-impact work aligned with the product vision and company strategy.
* Define and communicate product requirements, priorities, business outcomes, and release objectives.
* Act as the voice of the customer and target market for Product Development and cross-functional teams.
* Work closely with Engineering Managers to ensure teams iterate quickly to make the product more competitive and valuable.
* Partner closely with Product Development throughout discovery, validation, delivery, and iteration cycles.
* Coach and mentor other Product Managers, sharing frameworks and best practices that raise the bar across the product team.

* Communicate product strategy, roadmap updates, and priorities effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences, including company leadership.

**Thank you for considering a career at Ensemble!**

Ensemble is a leading provider of technology-enabled revenue cycle management solutions for health systems, including hospitals and affiliated physician groups. They offer end-to-end revenue cycle solutions as well as a comprehensive suite of point solutions to clients across the country.

Ensemble keeps communities healthy by keeping hospitals healthy. We recognize that healthcare requires a human touch, and we believe that every touch should be meaningful. This is why our people are the most important part of who we are. By empowering them to challenge the status quo, we know they will be the difference!

O.N.E Purpose:

* **Customer Obsession:** Consistently provide exceptional experiences for our clients, patients, and colleagues by understanding their needs and exceeding their expectations.
* **Embracing New Ideas:** Continuously innovate by embracing emerging technology and fostering a culture of creativity and experimentation.
* **Striving for Excellence:** Execute at a high level by demonstrating our “Best in KLAS” Ensemble Difference Principles and consistently delivering outstanding results.

**The Opportunity:**

**Welcome to Orchestration Works — Ensemble's bold leap into the future of healthcare innovation.**

We're building something big. Orchestration Works is a brand-new division designed to move fast, break barriers, and bring cutting-edge technology like AI and automation to life across the healthcare revenue cycle. This is where ideas don't just get tested — they get scaled. Our mission is simple: transform how we work, deliver next-level results for our clients, and lead the industry into tomorrow.

**Why Orchestration Works Exists**

Healthcare is changing at warp speed. To stay ahead, we're taking R+D out of the lab and putting it into real operations — quickly, intelligently, and boldly. This new division gives us the freedom and focus to experiment, learn, and deploy innovations that make a measurable impact.

**What Makes It Different**

* **A dedicated R+D powerhouse:** A 50-person independent team headquartered in Austin, Texas — built to move at startup speed.
* **Real autonomy:** Independent leadership, resources, and decision-making authority that lets us innovate without friction.
* **A laser focus:** Revenue Cycle Management innovations powered by automation, AI, and reimagined processes — including work on advanced Administrative and Clinical Reasoning Models.
* **A future-ready mindset:** We're here to help Ensemble evolve rapidly while protecting what makes us exceptional.

**Why It Matters**

The future of healthcare isn't waiting — and neither are we. Orchestration Works positions Ensemble to stay ahead of industry shifts, unlock new performance breakthroughs, and deliver smarter, faster, more reliable results for the organizations we serve.

### **Position Overview**

The Head of Product owns product practice for Orchestration Works: the intake funnel that feeds the portfolio, the ROI thesis discipline that every initiative must carry, and the operating cadence that keeps the 120-day model honest. Every problem that enters OW arrives with a documented hypothesis about automation lift, operational improvement, and financial return — this role is the keeper of that discipline, from intake through gate decisions through outcome reporting.

This is end-to-end initiative ownership across the pod portfolio: product leadership, outcomes, testing, and the reporting rhythm that keeps executive governance informed. The Head of Product runs the gate review cadence for the General Manager, owns portfolio reporting into Control Tower, and sets the product and design standard that pod Product Managers and Designers work to. The role is the interface to Ensemble's Product organization, ensuring OW's portfolio stays connected to the enterprise roadmap without duplicating it.

jobs.title: Head of Product
jobs.desc:
**About Finario**

Finario is a fast-growing SaaS company providing intelligent capital planning and portfolio strategy solutions to leading industrial enterprises worldwide. A few numbers worth knowing:

* **Revenue is strong and accelerating:** Real sustainable growth, not a story built on burn rate
* **Purpose-built product:** Finario is one of the first platforms built specifically for enterprise Capex. True specialist focus in one category
* **Trusted by billion-dollar enterprises**: Notable clients include Amway, Bausch + Lomb, and Sephora; all run their capital planning on Finario
* I**nvesting in innovation:** Finario has built its own purpose-built AI (Finario Predict) for capital project forecasting and benchmarking, so you'd be joining a product team that's actively pushing the category forward, not maintaining a legacy tool
* **High-stakes work:** this is core infrastructure for finance and ops leaders, not a nice-to-have. Our platform directly shapes how enterprises decide where to put hundreds of millions of dollars in capital investment

**About the Role**

**Team Overview**

Reporting to the CEO, the Head of Product plays a critical role at the intersection of clients, prospects, partners and our internal sales, marketing, support and engineering teams to continue driving growth in the marketplace.

**Position Overview**

As the Head of Product you will apply your product savvy and management insight to lead the continued evolution and development of the product to maintain and expand upon our position of market leadership. This position is based in Stamford, CT with our offices directly across from the train station.

**What you’ll do:**

* **Own the Roadmap**: One that the executive team and customers believe in, tied to measurable revenue and retention goals.
* **Ship great product:** Ensure that we make the most of our engineering efforts, releasing the most valuable and well-conceived new features to delight customers and drive market growth. Enable faster release cycles and higher feature adoption across key accounts
* **Lead product strategy:** Analyze and interpret market trends, competitive forces and technical developments in order to optimize new product development, differentiation and pricing.

jobs.title: Director of Product
jobs.desc:
**About Volley**
================

Volley Automation is building the future of parking through fully automated robotic parking systems. Our mission is to create sustainable parking solutions that are compact, efficient, and adaptable throughout a building’s lifecycle, while making EV charging easier and more accessible.

Are you intrigued by the idea of putting cars away with robots? Do you hate parking? Do you love parking? If so, we’d love to talk.

Volley Automation builds fully automated parking. Drivers hand off their car at the entry bay and walk away. From there the building takes over: AGVs move vehicles on trays, vertical conveyors move them between floors, and a controls and software stack orchestrates everything. The result is a garage that fits more cars into less concrete, in exactly the urban cores where parking is most expensive to build. Our systems go into real buildings, on real construction schedules, with real occupancy dates. That constraint shapes everything about how we build, develop, and engineer our product.

**The Role**
------------

* Turn customer and market evidence into product decisions: segment definition, configuration and pricing structure, feature go/no-go. Evidence means site visits, operator and owner interviews, and win/loss definitions and not a survey deck someone else built
* Articulate a product vision and get a company that does not yet agree to align behind it, in front of the executive team, the board, customers, and all the way through the entire org - especially the engineering team. You have held the line against per-project one-offs quietly becoming the product

* Experience with a product where the buyer and the user are different people with different definitions of value (developer and owner on one side, driver or parking spot owner/user on the other)
* Has owned a product's direction as well as its delivery. Can point to a roadmap you authored rather than inherited, and explain what you cut and why as well as what was executed on and why
* Owns a cross-functional development roadmap and plan spanning engineering, operations, commercial, and finance with time estimates that are aggressive and still real. Experience delivering this roadmap against an externally fixed date (construction schedule, customer opening, capital project milestone), where the date does not move because a certain department needs or wants it to
* Runs dependency mapping, critical path, and a risk register as habits, with suppliers, contract manufacturers, integrators, and long-lead components tracked as schedule dependencies
* Can close the loop from our Denver HQ and field deployments by turning commissioning, operational friction, and customer feedback into requirements and backlog items

**Required qualifications**
---------------------------

* 8+ years combined, with real depth on both sides of the product owner and program execution fronts. At least 3 years owning a product and at least 3 years owning a program outcome, which may overlap
* Experience with product definition and/or technical program execution with AGVs, AMRs, robotics, material handling, warehouse automation, or vertical transportation
* BS in engineering (ME, EE, or CS) or equivalent hands-on background. Must be able to read an architecture, interrogate a design decision, and push back credibly on a technical effort estimate
* Commercially literate enough to be believed by the CEO and the board: argues a feature in dollars, payback, and segment access
* Startup mode: ambiguity, thin process, influence over authority
* Travel roughly 25-35% for customers, suppliers, and installations

**Desired qualifications**
--------------------------

* Capital equipment product management: long sales cycles, six and seven figure deals, pricing and configuration structure, service and warranty definitions
* Ran a design partner program, customer advisory board, or equivalent structured voice-of-customer mechanism

**Role Summary**
----------------

Some of Temporal's most important product work begins inside Engineering. It may span the server, Cloud infrastructure, security, capacity, core primitives, SDKs, developer tooling, and AI without arriving as a finished market-facing roadmap. We need a senior product marketing leader who can earn Engineering's trust, understand what is coming, and decide which capabilities require positioning, technical proof, a launch, or a focused adoption plan.

Working directly with the VP of Product Marketing, you will own product-facing Product Marketing across Cloud and platform architecture, Core and SDKs, developer experience, and AI. You will manage a Principal-level Product Marketing Engineer and a Staff Product Marketing Engineer. You will also work closely with Product, Engineering, Developer Relations, Documentation, Sales, Solutions Architecture, and the Solutions and GTM Director.

This is a working leader role. You will personally lead the most important product and portfolio narratives, launch decisions, and adoption programs with the VP. You will set priorities across the portfolio and bring Product Marketing into roadmap discussions early enough to affect the outcome. As the product and market change, you will adjust the team's priorities without losing ownership of the work already underway.

**What You Will Do**
--------------------

* Build direct, durable relationships with engineering leaders and individual engineers across Temporal, including technical areas that do not have dedicated Product Management coverage.
* Maintain a clear view of the Product and Engineering roadmap. Assess each capability against customer need, market opportunity, competitive context, and GTM importance. Decide what requires research, positioning, technical proof, adoption guidance, a launch, or no external announcement.
* Create and run Temporal's monthly edition and special edition launch process, including launch tiering, calendar, audience, narrative, proof, asset requirements, decision points, and cross-functional ownership.
* Own product and portfolio positioning across Temporal's open-source technology, Cloud offering, core primitives, SDKs, pre-deployment and production features, and AI capabilities.
* Explain the customer value of work on reliability, scalability, performance, availability, security, capacity, migration, and developer tooling without overstating or simplifying the claims.
* Write and edit the positioning and messaging for the company's most important products and launches. Set the quality bar for product narratives across the team.
* Own customer interviews as part of Product Marketing's rotating case-study program and set the quality bar for the team. Capture the customer's problem, decision, implementation, and results. Use that evidence in launches, adoption programs, and recommendations to Product and Engineering.
* Hire, develop, and set priorities for the Product Marketing Engineers. Give them the access and authority to investigate important technical questions and turn their findings into proof, launch and adoption guidance, and specific product feedback.
* Own Temporal's technology ecosystem strategy. Decide which partner categories and integrations matter, set the portfolio narrative, and coordinate joint launches with Product, Engineering, Business Development, the Product Marketing Engineers, and the Solutions and GTM Director.
* Meet customers regularly at least 3 to 4 customers per month.
* Regularly supporting strategic sales deals and collaborating with key sales stakeholders.
* Make clear tradeoffs. Decide which launches need a full company motion, which need focused technical communication, and which do not need a launch at all.

-----------------------

jobs.desc:
**Company Description**

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

 **Job Description**

***Who*** **We're Looking For:**

We are looking for a Director of Product Management to lead a team of PMs as well as own the product strategy for empowering developers on the Now platform to build and take their applications to production faster. These areas include developer reach, testing, sandboxing, metering, and deployment of AI and human generated code.

As agentic build tools compress the time it takes to author a change, the bottleneck moves downstream. Testing and deploying safely to production is already one of the loudest customer asks and one of the sharpest pain points on the platform. When changes originate from agents as well as people, and arrive at a much higher rate, the ability to validate and trust them quickly stops being a quality-of-life improvement and becomes a precondition for platform growth. You will lead the team that enables this for developers.

This is not four adjacent feature areas with a shared manager. Customers experience the SDLC as one motion, and the central product challenge of this role is the connective tissue: a sandbox that behaves like the instance you will deploy to, a test suite that knows what changed, a release path that carries the evidence, and a model for building directly in production that an admin can actually govern. You set the strategy that makes their roadmaps resolve into a single lifecycle rather than four products that ship past each other.

The scope is deeply technical and close to execution. The Developer Reach feature area alone unlocks a path to building in production that admins can manage at scale without losing control, and it demands real technical depth to steer. You will also carry a broad surface, over twenty product areas, with the escalation volume that comes with it, and you will need to run that operational load without letting it consume the strategic work.

**What you get to do in this role:**

* Own the multi-year product strategy and roadmap across Developer Reach, Developer Sandboxes, Agentic Testing, and Release Ops, and define how they compose into one lifecycle from authored change to governed, audited deployment.
* Build, lead, and develop a team of PMs, one per area. Set a clear standard for product craft, coach PMs on strategy and execution, and hold the bar on the seams between them: shared primitives, consistent models, and a single coherent customer narrative.
* Set product direction for validating AI-originated change at scale: what it means to trust an agent's output, what evidence a release needs to carry, and how much of the test and review burden can be automated without losing accountability.
* Drive the Developer Reach strategy, including the product model for building in production with admin control, guardrails, and reversibility at enterprise scale.
* Define the sandbox strategy: provisioning speed, production parity, data handling, and the developer experience of getting a safe place to work in seconds rather than days.
* Own the release governance path end to end, including the tradeoffs between developer velocity and auditability, and the gating model that makes those tradeoffs explicit rather than accidental.
* Shape the metering and cost-modeling strategy for this area in partnership with Pricing & Packaging and Finance, and underst

The Colorado Benefits Eligibility and Enrollment Systems (CoBEES) is a cross-agency portfolio of information technology systems, subsystems, applications, interfaces, training, and communications managed and maintained by the State of Colorado to deliver access to public assistance and medical coverage programs for Coloradans. **Our Mission**
---------------

As the world’s number 1 job site\*, our mission is to help people get jobs. We strive to cultivate an inclusive and accessible workplace where all people feel comfortable being themselves. We're looking to grow our teams with more people who share our enthusiasm for innovation and creating the best experience for job seekers.

--------------

As a Director of Product Management for Candidate Trust & Evaluation, you will manage a team of product managers who collectively own screening: the portfolio that drives return on investment from the moment a candidate clicks the Apply button. That work spans screener questions, AI evaluation, candidate trust (including verifications and related signals), and automations such as AI Recruiter and automated interview scheduling.

You will set and continuously refine strategy for the domain, translating company and business-unit goals into a clear, coherent screening portfolio, and holding your team accountable for outcomes that improve screening ROI and ladder up to those goals.

You will partner closely with Engineering, Design, Data Science, and business leadership to align on priorities, resources, and sequencing across these products. You bring deep experience across AI, trust, and hiring automation, and you use that breadth to shape both what the organization bets on and how your teams operate. You will hire, develop, and coach product managers at every level, building career paths that grow senior ICs and future product leaders. Your leadership will ensure screening creates meaningful, balanced value for employers and candidates with aligned incentives that strengthen hiring outcomes over time.

jobs.title: Director of Product
jobs.desc:
Courier Health is on a mission to solve one of the biggest and most meaningful opportunities in healthcare: reinvent how people living with chronic and rare diseases are supported.

We are building the future of patient engagement for life sciences companies. Our software is leveraged by biopharma companies to support patients in their complex journey from diagnosis to initiating and remaining on therapy to achieve optimal health outcomes.

### **Come Build with Us**

We're a NYC-based team that believes culture, craft, and customer obsession go hand in hand. We show up for each other the same way we show up for the people we serve. We're an office-first company that values in-person collaboration 4 days per week because we believe the best work happens when you can collaborate and brainstorm together in the same room. If that sounds like your kind of place, we think you'll love it here.

### **The Opportunity**

Courier Health is at an inflection point. We exist to get patients faster, better access to life-saving therapies, and product helps to shape decisions related to which patients we reach next and how soon.

As Director of Product, you will lead a team of product managers covering the full platform, reporting directly to the CEO. You will also keep a hand in the work running discovery, writing the spec, making the call — on the bets that matter most.

The roadmap here is not handed down. You will decide what we build, in what order, and what we deliberately don't do, in a market where the right answer is rarely obvious and the stakes are patients starting therapy. If you have led product teams inside someone else's operating model and want to define your own, this is the seat.

### **What You'll Build**

**A product team that makes its own calls.** You will coach to a standard in weekly one on ones and roadmap reviews, raise the bar on writing and discovery, and give your PMs enough room to be wrong and get better. The goal is a team that can size a bet and defend it without you in the room.

**A roadmap the whole company can bet on.** Sales, implementation, and engineering all plan against what product says is coming. You will set the sequencing across a growing customer base, make the tradeoffs between what one strategic client needs and what the platform needs, and say no clearly enough that people trust the yes. Commitments hold, and when they change, everyone knows why in time to act.

**Discovery grounded in how patients actually get to therapy.** Our users are the people running patient support programs, field teams, and hub operations. You will get your team in front of them, translate what you hear into product, and build the customer and market fluency that makes our roadmap hard to copy. Strong opinions are welcome here. Strong opinions without customer contact are not.

### **What Makes You Successful**

* 10+ years in product management at a B2B software company, with a track record of shipping products enterprise customers renewed and expanded.
* 5+ years managing product managers. You have hired, coached, and given hard feedback that made someone better.
* Proven ownership of a roadmap end to end from customer discovery and strategy through launch and measured outcomes, not just execution against someone else's plan.
* Strong technical fluency. You can work through data models, API integrations, and architectural tradeoffs with engineers and hold your own. Coding is not required. Depth is.
* Excellent judgment under ambiguity. You can make a call with incomplete information, explain the reasoning, and change course without drama when the evidence shifts.
* Exceptional written communication. You think in documents, and your specs make the decision obvious.
* Comfortable working directly with senior customer stakeholders, including the conversations nobody wants to have.
* Experience building process where none existed, and the restraint to keep it minimal.

**Bonus points if you have:**

* Worked in healt

jobs.title: Director of Product Marketing
jobs.desc:
Proof is the world's first identity-assured transaction management platform and we are on a mission to digitize trust for all of life’s most critical transactions. Developed by the same market leaders and experts who brought notarization online with Notarize℠, Proof offers trust in a digital world by verifying identities and securing transactions to protect businesses and their customers. Since 2015, we’ve completed many of the world’s first digital commerce transactions, including the first online real estate closing, online mortgage closing, online auto sale, and online will and we're still just getting started!

Proof operates identity infrastructure for high-consequence transactions. Built on a WebTrust-audited certificate authority and PKI-anchored verifiable credentials, Proof helps more than 8,000 businesses, from financial institutions and mortgage lenders to insurers and wealth managers, verify who is on the other side of a transaction. Having created the online notarization category, we're now extending into portable digital identity with our Verifiable Digital Credential (VDC) for banks, and into authorization for AI agents.

As **Director of Product Marketing,** you'll turn that technical foundation into positioning that a bank's Chief Risk Officer, head of digital, and compliance team all understand and act on. Day to day, you'll work across Product, Sales, and Marketing to shape messaging, lead launches, equip Sales to win, and make sure the market sees Proof as the trusted identity layer. You'll also lead and develop the product marketing function, starting with the **Partner & Customer** **Marketing Manager.**

### **What you’ll do as the Director of Product Marketing at Proof:**

**Who we are:**

Motive empowers the people who run physical operations with tools to make their work safer, more productive, and more profitable. For the first time ever, safety, operations and finance teams can manage their drivers, vehicles, equipment, and fleet related spend in a single system. Combined with industry leading AI, the Motive platform gives you complete visibility and control, and significantly reduces manual workloads by automating and simplifying tasks.

Motive serves nearly 100,000 customers – from Fortune 500 enterprises to small businesses – across a wide range of industries, including transportation and logistics, construction, energy, field service, manufacturing, agriculture, food and beverage, retail, and the public sector.

Visit gomotive.com to learn more.

As Director of Product Strategy, Monetization & Operations, you will own the commercial and financial engine of Motive's R&D organization. You will lead revenue, pricing, packaging, margin, and cost-reduction efforts across Product and Engineering, and pair that near-term revenue strategy with the long-term product and company strategy that sets Motive's direction. You will report to the Sr. Director of Product, build your own team, and work daily with senior leaders across the company.

You are an exceptional partner and a rigorous analyst: someone who earns trust across Product, Engineering, Finance, and Go-to-Market, and who turns complex data into clear decisions.
